 From Hanbok-Wrapped Compacts to Ink-Inspired Eyeliner, HWIRAN Takes Korean Beauty to the World
 Posted November. 20, 2026 09:51,   
 Updated November. 20, 2026 09:52

 - South Korean beauty brand HWIRANcombines traditional Korean aesthetics with modern cosmetics, offering products inspired b y hanbok, plum blossoms, and Korean ink painting.
- HWIRAN is expanding into global markets, exporting to 12 countries and developing a wider range of makeup shades and products to meet diverse consumer preferences.
- HWIRAN aims to become a global K-beauty and cultural brand, strengthening international distribution and partnerships while bringing Korean heritage into everyday beauty routines. 
 Da-Hea Jung, CEO of HWIRAN / source = HWIRAN
K-beauty continues to grow worldwide. According to South Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, cosmetics exports reached $11.1 billion, or about 14.8 trillion won, in the first nine months of 2026, up 31.1% from a year earlier. The United States became the largest export market, accounting for 21.1% of the total, followed by China and Japan. That growth, however, has been uneven across product categories. In makeup, brands increasingly need to distinguish themselves by adapting to local skin tones, makeup routines and preferences for different formulations.
HWIRAN is a makeup and skincare brand that reinterprets traditional Korean aesthetics through modern cosmetics. Its products include cushion compacts covered in specially woven hanbok fabric, formulations made with plum blossom water and eyeliner inspired by the tonal variations of Korean ink painting. Those cultural references extend through the ingredients, formulations, packaging and the experience of using each product.
HWIRAN aims to become a global K-beauty company that brings Korean beauty into everyday life around the world, combining traditional aesthetics and cultural values with modern cosmetics technology and design. It has targeted international beauty markets since its founding and now exports to 12 countries. It is expanding distribution in major markets, including the United States.
 Bringing Korean aesthetics into everyday beauty routines 
Da-Hea Jung, CEO of HWIRAN, studied cosmetic pharmacology at Daegu Haany U
niversity and researched cosmetic ingredients and formulations in a university laboratory. She then spent about a decade in the cosmetics industry, including at startups, gaining experience in brand planning, product development, distribution and international business. “South Korean cosmetics have excellent manufacturing technology and competitive products, but I felt there were relatively few makeup brands that placed distinctly Korean aesthetics at the center of their identity,” she said.
“I built the brand around combining traditional Korean aesthetics with modern cosmetics technology,” Jung said. “We want consumers to experience Korean culture through our products and naturally share the stories and values behind them, taking traditional design beyond its visual role.”
From the hanbok-covered Maehwa Silk cusionto Sumuk Eyeliner 
 HWIRAN’s signature Maehwa Silk cusion / source = HWIRAN
HWIRAN’s signature products are Maehwa Silk cusion, Kombucha black tea sun serum and Sumuk Eyeliner. Their concepts draw, respectively, on hanbok and plum blossoms, fermentation traditions, and Korean ink painting. All products are developed according to vegan principles. Maehwa Silk cusion is designed to convey Korean beauty through sight and touch. Its defining feature is a compact covered in fabric specially woven for the product using hanbok textile techniques. Plum blossom motifs complement a formula containing plum blossom water that provides natural-looking coverage.
“We wanted people to feel Korean beauty at their fingertips, and that led us to hanbok, something quintessentially Korean,” Jung said. “We worked with a local business with 50 years of experience and with artisans. The fabric is dyed using the same process used to make hanbok before being applied to the compact.” She added, “Working with hanbok fabric made from fine threads and fitting it to a rigid compact is difficult. Completing a single product requires roughly 20 production steps.”
Kombucha black tea sun serum combines skincare with sun protection. It contains 14.9% fermented kombucha ingredients and has a thin, lightweight, serum-like texture designed to absorb quickly. “We designed it to keep makeup from pilling or sitting unevenly when sunscreen, skincare and makeup base are used together,” Jung said. “It provides sun protection and hydration in one step and feels comfortable under makeup.” The product was named an official KPGA sunscreen in April and is being supplied at tournament venues.
The latest addition, Sumuk Eyeliner, is a brush-tip eyeliner inspired by the ink tones and gradations of Korean ink painting. It comes in four shades—black, dark brown, brown and underliner. “We focused on achieving a clear line with one stroke and a color that deepens as you layer it,” Jung said. “Because it is used so close to the eyes, we included panthenol and biotin to provide eyelash care as well.” The packaging features artwork by an emerging designer, with the four versions forming a single continuous image.
 Korean influences extend to the ingredients 
HWIRAN connects Korean influences across its ingredients, formulations, packaging and the experience of using its products. Ingredients that grow naturally in Korea or have long been used there—including plum blossom water, fermented kombucha ingredients, bamboo extract and charcoal—inform its product concepts. Traditional aesthetics find expression in modern formulations and design.
Plum blossoms, for example, are one of the Four Gentlemen, a group of plants depicted in traditional painting. They symbolize resilience and integrity, flowering after enduring the winter cold. HWIRAN connects that symbolism to skin barrier care, using plum blossom water as a main ingredient in place of purified water. “We designed the formula to be gentle enough to use like skincare,” Jung said. “As more consumers use a single cushion compact to complete their base makeup, we also focused on making coverage buildable without feeling heavy or suffocating, even after several layers.”
HWIRAN has a dedicated research and development department to support product development and secure intellectual property rights. “Our direction is to become a global beauty brand that combines cultural identity, product performance and technological strength,” Jung said.
 Expanding beyond Asia with products tailored to local skin tones and retail markets 
 HWIRAN’s signature Sumuk Eyeliner / source = HWIRAN
HWIRAN has developed its business around growth in both South Korea and overseas. It now exports to 12 countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Türkiye, Cambodia, Canada, France and Australia. It is focusing on developing products and expanding its range to reflect diverse skin tones and consumer needs, as well as each country’s regulatory requirements.
Its distribution strategy also varies by market. HWIRAN is strengthening product localization, content marketing and strategic partnerships to match local shoppers and retail conditions and build its competitiveness worldwide. In Japan, its products are stocked at three Marui department stores, supported by online channels including Qoo10 and Rakuten. In China, it works with influencers known as wanghong through TikTok. In Malaysia, it supplies five department stores and shopping centers. In the United States, it has launched on online channels including Amazon and TikTok Shop, while aiming to place its products in about 80 small beauty stores.
The biggest challenge HWIRAN has identified internationally is shade selection. Its initial export expansion focused on Asia, particularly Southeast Asia, but discussions with buyers from Europe, the Middle East and India revealed greater demand for makeup suited to a wider range of skin tones. “We received positive feedback on how the products feel and their design, but some buyers said the shade selection was limited and the prices were somewhat high,” Jung said. “We are refining our shade range, starting with Maehwa Silk cusion, and aim to offer up to 13 shades, from fair to deep skin tones.”
HWIRAN plans to expand its makeup range to include concealers, foundations, lipsticks and lip tints, reflecting global beauty trends and local consumer preferences. For example, it plans to introduce richly pigmented lipsticks based on its assessment that lipstick remains popular overseas, while lip tints dominate in South Korea. It is also developing new skincare and fragrance lines inspired by the Four Gentlemen.
The company is also addressing regulatory requirements for entry into the United States. Focusing on Sumuk Eyeliner, HWIRANhas undertaken registration and related procedures under the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act, or MoCRA. The law establishes requirements including registration of facilities that manufacture or process cosmetics for the U.S. market and the submission of product listings.
Building international connections through SparkLabs 
 A promotional image for HWIRAN / source = HWIRAN
Founded in 2023, HWIRAN has continued to grow sales while expanding its international distribution network. In South Korea, it has sold primarily through its own online store and operated department store pop-ups, including at Hyundai Department Store, to reach more customers in person. It has secured investment from BlissVine Ventures and is preparing to raise additional funding. It is also going through the selection process for TIPS, a technology startup support program run by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups.
Through the Global Startup Academy, run by the Korea SMEs and Startups Agency, HWIRAN received support from program operator SparkLabs, including mentoring on global business strategy, help refining its business model and assistance building networks for overseas expansion. “That helped us review overseas distribution structures and localization strategies and define a clearer direction for our global business,” Jung said.
HWIRAN said its ambition extends beyond cosmetics to becoming a brand that represents Korean cultural values. “We want to grow into a global beauty brand where anyone in the world can choose products inspired by Korean aesthetics that suit their skin tone and taste, across countries and consumer groups,” Jung said. “Ultimately, we want HWIRAN to become a cultural brand that comes to mind when people think of Korea,” she added. “Our goal is to develop Korea’s cultural heritage into modern products and designs that consumers around the world can naturally experience in their daily lives.”
By Ye-ji Kim (yj@itdonga.com)
